A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Gaussian-Det. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables and figures, are readable and can be matched despite reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original detection experiments on 3D-FRONT and ScanNet, component ablations, efficiency measurements and qualitative analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains those original results and adds pose-noise experiments, reconstruction ablations and an instance-segmentation extension.

M1.justification: The main detector components and equations are retained. V2 additionally adapts surface-closure estimation to Gaussian-Grouping, supporting or suppressing segmented instances (Section 4.3). This is a limited procedural extension; the expanded detector architecture description does not establish a redesign.

E1.justification: V2 retains indoor object detection on 3D-FRONT and ScanNet but adds open-vocabulary 3D instance segmentation and detection with noisy camera poses. These substantially broaden task and input-condition coverage. The segmentation dataset is not identified.

E2.justification: The detection comparator sets are retained. New Table 6 substantially expands comparisons into segmentation, reporting DEVA, LERF, SA3D, LangSplat and Gaussian-Grouping against the closure-enhanced approach; none appeared in v1's evaluated comparisons.

E3.justification: Existing detection budgets, preprocessing and AP/AR thresholds remain unchanged. Added experiments introduce camera-extrinsic perturbations with mean zero and variance 0.07, alternative 3DGS/2DGS reconstruction settings, and segmentation mIoU/mBIoU and resource measurements. These are additions to experimental settings, not documented revisions of the retained experiments.

E4.justification: V2 adds substantive tests of sensitivity to camera-pose errors and dependence on the underlying Gaussian reconstruction (Table 5 and Appendix C.3). It also adds qualitative component-ablation and challenging-case comparisons. The original component ablations, hyperparameter sweep and training curves remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, evaluation seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The retained closure histograms and probabilistic feature modeling do not constitute new uncertainty reporting for experimental results.

E6.justification: Existing detection and ablation scores remain unchanged, but substantial results are added. Table 5 reports noisy-pose AP25 of 81.5 for Gaussian-Det versus 67.6 for G-BRNet. Table 6 reports segmentation mIoU/mBIoU of 76.5/73.3 versus Gaussian-Grouping's 69.7/67.9. Tables 9 and 11 add reconstruction-variant scores and segmentation efficiency measurements, respectively.

T1.justification: The flux theorem, surface-normal derivation and variational-loss derivation are mathematically retained. The theorem's existing proof moves from Section 3.3 to Appendix B.4. Expanded geometric explanations and differentiated pooling notation do not introduce new theoretical results.

C1.justification: The abstract and main conclusion retain the same claims about continuous surface representation, CIM-based proposal refinement and superior detection performance. The introduction clarifies the closure prior without redefining the headline contributions.

C2.justification: V2 interprets the added experiments as supporting robustness to pose noise and transfer of the closure prior to segmentation, and discusses reconstruction-quality sensitivity. Existing occlusion and joined-object limitations remain. Future work replaces the proposed reconstruction-quality application with exploration of autonomous-driving datasets.

D1.justification: Appendix B.1 newly specifies PointNet++ sampling layers, feature dimensions, the 128/128/9 refinement MLP and Gaussian attributes supplied to point-cloud baselines. These are additional implementation disclosures. Table 11 also supplies segmentation training-time and GPU-memory measurements.

R1.justification: V2 adds references covering Gaussian novel-view synthesis, variational autoencoders, 2DGS and the new segmentation comparators. The existing positioning of continuous surface modeling against discrete point/volume-based detection remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: Selective rewrites clarify feature extraction and CIM's flux weighting. Related-work subsections become paragraph headings, qualitative and failure discussions are reordered, and appendices are reorganized with the proof relocated. Most existing prose, including the abstract and main conclusion, is retained.

P2.justification: V2 redraws the framework and closure-prior diagrams, moves Figure 1 before the abstract, recolors and reduces the main qualitative grid, and relocates closure histograms to the appendix. New segmentation, dataset, ablation and robustness visuals, together with four additional tables, substantially revise the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: The pose-noise and reconstruction ablations test weaknesses unexamined in v1, while Appendix B.1 improves implementation transparency. These strengthen evidential support and reproducibility. The main detection evidence remains unchanged, and missing dataset and procedural details limit the weight of the new segmentation study, supporting a limited overall improvement.
